absent_or_gaps.why: the page's Ultrafast table lists gpt-6.1-sol and not gpt-6-luna; not used by the study

the page gives no per-token cache-write price for either model, only a context caching (read) price and an hourly storage price; lead ruling 3 sets the candidate's value equal to the input price (written tokens billed as input); that is the lead's ruling, not page wording

candidate_marks.anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: admitted for sub-agents only (not a registered model); prompts up to 100,000 tokens
candidate_marks.google/gemini-3.8-flash: re-read on the run day: current price (through 31 Dec 2026); the candidate takes the price in force on the day the Gemini arm runs, which Javier's later word sets
candidate_marks.google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite: re-read on the run day: Gemini runs only on Javier's later word

lead_rulings: 1. Anthropic cache write: both rows kept (5-minute, 1-hour); the candidate takes the 1-hour price, the higher one, as a conservative bound.
2. OpenAI cache write: both rows kept (30-minute, 12-hour); the candidate takes the 12-hour price, the higher one, as a conservative bound.

3. Google cache write: the candidate sets cache_creation_input_tokens equal to the input price (written tokens are billed as input). This is the lead's ruling, not wording on Google's page, which gives no per-token write price.
4. OpenAI calls over 272K input tokens. The candidate holds the standard price. The cost step (L4) prices any call over 272K input tokens at its long-context row and flags it in the results.

5. gemini-3.8-flash: both prices stay in the table, and the candidate holds today's price, marked re-read on the run day. The frozen table holds today's gemini-3.8-flash price. If the Gemini arm runs on or after 1 Jan 2027, its cost is re-priced at the then-current row and published as a declared deviation.

residuals.what: Google hourly cache storage stays out of the per-token schema
page_quotes: gemini-3.5-flash-lite: "Not available $0.03 $1.00 / 1,000,000 tokens per hour (storage price)"

gemini-3.8-flash: "Free of charge $0.075 through December 31, 2026. $0.15 starting January 1, 2027. $0.50 / 1,000,000 tokens per hour (storage price) through December 31, 2026. $1.00 / 1,000,000 tokens per hour (storage price) starting January 1, 2027."

Arm O (Codex) billing: its rows are API-equivalent, not billed. routing.json (spend_cap_markers_status) says, of 13 Oct, 'when arm O moved from an API key to a ChatGPT subscription sign-in', and 'a ChatGPT sign-in bills no money per call unless the account holds purchased credits'; the owner confirms Codex2 holds no purchased credits before the first Codex walk (B8 precondition)

claude-haiku-5-5 is admitted for sub-agents only (claude_code_adapter.py and check_take.py SUBAGENT_EXPLICIT_MODELS), not a registered model; the candidate holds its prompts-up-to-100,000-tokens row, and the page prices a request over 100,000 prompt tokens at a higher row (kept in the table). Pricing such a sub-agent call at that row is not yet ruled

follow_ups_for_L4: Where the take records split cache writes by duration (Anthropic usage reports ephemeral_5m and ephemeral_1h input tokens), the cost step prices each part at its own row; the same for OpenAI 30-minute and 12-hour writes.
The cost step (L4) prices any call over 272K input tokens at its long-context row and flags it in the results.
The frozen table holds today's gemini-3.8-flash price. If the Gemini arm runs on or after 1 Jan 2027, its cost is re-priced at the then-current row and published as a declared deviation.
Adapter-recorded model ids must equal the registered ids (costs.account looks prices up by exact id), and Codex's service_tier tells the tier.
Rule whether a claude-haiku-5-5 sub-agent call over 100,000 prompt tokens is priced at the page's over-100,000 row (not yet ruled).
